name: NeWA Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Three reigns survive, none from the fed's own Title History page alone: Mac Michaels was already champion by 17 January 1999, when Lycos took the title from him by pinfall with a foreign object (a "slap jack"); the fed's own News page (27 January 1999) still bills Lycos as reigning "Mid-Atlantic Champion," submitted for a unification match at the NeWA PPV Lord of the Rings; no document says how or when that reign ended.

name: Mid-Atlantic Tag Team Titles
epitaph: The fed's own Title History page attests one reign: Angels of the Night won this belt in a Four Corners Match, 10 February 1999. The same team name holds the BCW National Tag Team Championship on the NeWA hub's own British sister territory; the two are read together as the same touring team rather than a coincidence (see this wing's own Affiliations). The fed's own News page (27 January 1999) implies an earlier reign this holding does not otherwise attest, asking rhetorically whether the champions have defended "even once since Crowing Event" [sic] — no date, match, or result survives for that named event, an honest gap, not resolved here. No later change survives.

name: Mid-Atlantic Television Title
epitaph: The fed's own News page (27 January 1999) has Jim Crockett, Jr. Fred Rogers is next attested champion by 10 February 1999, per the fed's own Title History page, via a Three Way Elimination Match rather than any resolution of the ordered series — no document says who else stood in that match, or how or when the vacancy the strip created was filled before it.

name: Mid-Atlantic Light-Heavyweight Title
epitaph: Ryan Carling won this title vacant in a Triangle Match, 15 January 1999, and retained it in a Four Corners Match two nights later — the only reign this holding attests. The fed's own Title History page names no title of this exact name, only an empty "Mid-Atlantic Light-Weight Title" row with no entries; almost certainly the same belt under a variant spelling, not reconciled here.
